decisions.decision: What is the source of the audit?
decisions.ruling: Audit docs/setup/tools.md against the current macos/tools/. The Notes of the deleted macos-setup docs/tool-reference.md (lines 71-201 at commit a4ec825^) are a checklist, not a source: each claim that is still true must be in the doc, and a false claim is dropped.
decisions.rejected: Copy the true Notes word for word into a bootstrap doc: about a third of the claims are false now, and that source finds no other drift of the doc.

decisions.decision: How far does the audit go?
decisions.ruling: All the ### <tool> sections of docs/setup/tools.md (110 on 2026-11-28), plus its sections 'How a tool works' and 'The packs'. Each section is compared with tools.toml, files/, tasks/ and scripts/ of its tool folder, and 'The packs' with macos/packs.toml.
decisions.rejected: Only the about 20 sections that the Notes touch. Also fix the stale comments in the tool files (parked in docs/memory/gaps/2026-11-28-mac-tool-stale-comments-parked.md, because they change shipped files).

decisions.ruling: Each fact goes in the ### section of the tool that owns it. A rule for many tools goes in 'How a tool works', as a paragraph before the item legend ('Each section below gives these items for one tool:').
decisions.rejected: A separate ## Notes section in docs/setup/tools.md: the facts are then in two places. docs/design/mac.md: tool details do not belong in a design doc.

decisions.decision: Does the plan wait for other plans?
decisions.ruling: It requires docs/plans/2026-11-27-tool-skills, which requires 2026-11-27-tool-selection and 2026-11-27-mac-backup-target. The audit then examines the final state of macos/tools/ after the three plans. Each claim of the survey is examined again at run time, because those plans can change it.
decisions.rejected: Require nothing: the audit then examines a state that changes, the doc drifts again, and the landings can conflict in docs/setup/tools.md.

decisions.ruling: Audit in parallel, then apply once: U1 to U5 (wave 1) each write one findings file in docs/plans/2026-11-28-mac-tools-doc-audit/audit/ and edit nothing else; U6 (wave 2) applies the five files to docs/setup/tools.md. The audit files stay in the plan folder as the record of the audit.
decisions.rejected: Four serial waves that each edit a part of the doc directly: about four times slower. One unit for the whole doc: about 110 tool folders and 1253 lines of doc are too much for one context.

decisions.decision: How are the tools split between the four parts?
decisions.ruling: By the name of the tool folder, in LC_ALL=C sort order: part A is each name up to and including dprint; part B is each name from duplicate-detective up to and including mas; part C is each name from microsoft-excel up to and including ssh; part D is each name from starship on. A tool that a later plan adds or removes falls in its range by sort order. A tool with a folder and no section, or a section and no folder, belongs to the part of its name.
decisions.rejected: Fixed line ranges of the doc: they change when 2026-11-27-tool-skills lands.

decisions.ruling: Each finding gives the section, the kind (wrong, missing, extra, order), the current text of the doc (or 'none'), the evidence as file:line, and the full correct text that U6 writes. The evidence is in macos/tools/ or macos/packs.toml; for a finding of How a tool works it can also be in docs/design/ or cli/. A finding with no evidence is not written. A missing section and a section with no tool folder are findings too. The kind order covers a section out of sort order and an item out of the order of the legend inside one section. A new text of more than one line (a whole section, an item with a sub-list) goes in a fenced markdown block, indented under its finding, in place of the quoted new text.
decisions.rejected: Free notes: U6 then has to examine the tool folders again.

decisions.decision: What is the style of the new text?
decisions.ruling: New text follows the existing doc: the items of the legend in 'How a tool works' (Packs, Stage, Depends, Files, Tasks, Scripts, Contributes to, Defaults, Mise sections, Question), in that order, and the plain STE prose of the doc (ASD-STE100: short sentences, simple present, active voice). A 'why' rule is one or two sentences in the prose paragraph under the ### heading, after the first sentence. No secret value is written: a secret is named by its variable name only.
decisions.rejected: Copy the long prose of the old Notes.

decisions.decision: What happens to a stale comment in a tool file?
decisions.ruling: No unit changes a file of macos/tools/. An audit unit lists each stale comment that it finds in the '## Stale comments' section of its audit file. U6 does not apply them. The parked item docs/memory/gaps/2026-11-28-mac-tool-stale-comments-parked.md takes them, and its later change plan reads the audit files.
decisions.rejected: Fix the comments in this plan: that changes shipped files, which is not a docs change.

decisions.decision: Can an audit unit edit the doc or the tools?
decisions.ruling: No. U1 to U5 read docs/setup/tools.md, macos/tools/, macos/packs.toml, the docs of docs/design/ and, for How a tool works, cli/; they write only their own audit file.
decisions.rejected: Let each audit unit edit its own sections: two units of one wave cannot own the same file.

decisions.ruling: teams. An audit unit that finds a fact that belongs to another part can send it to the unit of that part. Talk is a help only: each unit file stands alone.
decisions.rejected: solo: no technical reason forces it.

decisions.ruling: No. The plan lands no runnable code, only docs, so the wave review is the only check.
decisions.rejected: A review unit: it has no code to review.
A cheaper tier for the audit units: the audit must read code and templates correctly.

decisions.decision: How does U6 resolve two findings for the same text?
decisions.ruling: The evidence in macos/tools/ decides. When a part audit (U1 to U4) and the general audit (U5) give text for the same section, U6 writes one text that holds the facts of both, with no repeated sentence. When two findings contradict each other, U6 reads the cited lines and writes the text that the files support.
decisions.rejected: The later unit wins: the order of the units has no relation to which finding is correct.

decisions.decision: What state does a checklist claim get when only a part of it has evidence, or when it is already stated in a doc other than docs/setup/tools.md?
decisions.ruling: A claim with a part that has no evidence in the files is stated with the proven part only, and its line names the dropped part with the reason (for example C2, C4, C12). A claim that a bootstrap doc already states is stated — already in <doc> <section>, and that doc can be another doc than docs/setup/tools.md (for example C14, docs/design/mac.md). A claim that the doc states in part (for example C24) is stated with new text for the rest only, and its line names the section that already holds the first part.
decisions.rejected: Drop the whole claim: the proven part is then lost. A third state partly: it adds a case to each check for no gain.

decisions.decision: What happens to an item of a section that the legend does not name (for example Runtime:, Settings:, Folder mode:, Manual step:, Trust paths:, Question `<key>`:, Contributes to `<tool>`:)?
decisions.ruling: Keep an item when the files support it. Each item kind that occurs in more than one section, and the forms Question `<key>`: and Contributes to `<tool>`:, gets a line in the legend of How a tool works: U5 finds these kinds with a grep of the whole doc and writes the legend lines. The form Question `<key>`: takes the place of Question, and Contributes to `<tool>`: the place of Contributes to; each other new kind goes after Mise sections and before Question, in the order that U5 gives in the legend. For a kind that occurs in one section only, the part unit of that section decides: keep it when it names a real part of the tool (for example Manual step:), else move its text into the prose paragraph of the section, as a finding of kind wrong. An item that the files do not support is a finding of kind wrong or extra.
decisions.rejected: Report each extra item as extra and move its text into the prose: the prose gets long and the clear labels are lost. Keep all and change nothing: the legend stays wrong.

decisions.decision: Does mise give --all to the task in a gate line such as mise run code:format --all, with no -- separator? (rulings review round 4)
decisions.ruling: Yes. Keep the gate lines as written. A test on 2026-11-28 with mise 2026.11.14: mise run code:format --all --debug printed 5920 lines, mise run code:format -- --all --debug 5916, and mise run code:format --debug 132. A flag after the task name goes to the task. CLAUDE.md uses the same form (mise run test --all).
decisions.rejected: Write each gate line as mise run <task> -- --all: the result is the same, and the form differs from the repo and the other plans.

decisions.decision: Q1: Should the audit keep, drop, or mark as owner knowledge the claims of docs/setup/tools.md that no file of macos/tools/ proves and none contradicts (the openwhispr Manual step details, the mise CLI item on owner patterns)?
decisions.ruling: Keep them unchanged. The openwhispr Manual steps and the mise owner-pattern item stay as they are.
decisions.rejected: drop them as findings of kind extra; keep them and mark them as owner knowledge in the prose

decisions.decision: Q2: What value should the Stage item of the bash, fish and zsh sections show, given stage = "init" in tools.toml and the legend value `migrate`?
decisions.ruling: Keep `migrate` in all three sections (bash, fish, zsh), drop a.md F2, and apply the reworded legend of G2 (`migrate` for a tool with stage = "init").
decisions.rejected: Change all three sections to `init` and rewrite the legend item as the stage value of tools.toml
